routes.statement: Exactly one <main> element is visible; any other carries the hidden attribute, or is hidden from assistive technologies by a style, keeping in mind that a style alone does not keep the visible <main> unique when style sheets are disabled.

citations.quote: Si le document possède plusieurs éléments `<main>`, vérifier qu’un seul de ces éléments est visible (les autres occurrences de l’élément sont pourvues d’un attribut `hidden`) ;
les autres devant disposer d’un attribut `hidden` ou d’un style permettant de les masquer aux technologies d’assistances
l’utilisation d’un style seul restera insuffisante pour assurer l’unicité d’une balise `<main>` visible en cas de désactivation des feuilles de styles

rationale.text: The wording lists six conditions that must all hold, so each is a requirement. The particular case makes the criterion not applicable when the declared doctype is not the HTML5 doctype; it is listed as an exception on each requirement. Four requirements need judgment: which part of a page is its header zone, its navigation zones or its footer zone, and whether a given <nav> holds a main or secondary navigation, cannot be decided by code. The glossary itself warns that the header and footer zones are not to be confused with any content marked up with <header> or <footer>. The wording names elements only, <header>, <nav>, <main> and <footer>; it accepts no ARIA role in their place, unlike the wording of 9.1 and 9.3. The candidate is none. Two custom checks look at the two remaining requirements, and both faults are evidence only. First, custom/9-2-main-missing faults an HTML5 page with no <main> element, no main role and no frame, when some visible, exposed text lies outside header, footer, nav, aside and dialog elements and their role equivalents. That does not prove the page has a main content zone left unstructured. The glossary identifies the main zone by the page's principal content and excludes menus, search and secondary content; text left outside the identified landmarks can still be secondary. Codex's example is an interim shell with its header and navigation marked up, a search or related-notice area in a plain div, and no principal content: the residual text trips the check although it is not the main zone. Whether every HTML5 page must have a visible <main> whatever it holds would need a ruling, which has not been made. Second, custom/9-2-main-multiple-shown faults two <main> elements that it counts as shown. Its definition of shown checks the hidden attribute, the accessibility tree, visibility, opacity, clip and geometry, but not masking: a second main with ordinary text and an all-transparent mask-image, opacity 1, visibility visible and intact geometry is counted as shown although nothing of it is painted. So the check does not prove that two <main> elements are visible at once. Both links keep their routes and their scope and become evidence_only. Neither check answers no_fault. What would raise the entry: for the main zone, a ruling that a visible <main> is required on every HTML5 page, or a way to establish that the residual text is principal content; for the single main, a definition of shown that establishes paint (mask, filter, blend, transparent fill and the like) separately from visibility and exposure, with fixtures for ordinary visible, hidden and masked mains. Both checks read the doctype first: no declared doctype gives cannot_tell, since the particular case does not say whether a page without one falls under it; a declared doctype other than the HTML5 one gives inapplicable. axe's region rule is tagged but not linked: it is best-practice, it asks that all content sit in some landmark, and it accepts ARIA landmark roles in place of the elements the wording names, so it examines none of the six conditions. Applicability is judgment: not applicable follows from the declared doctype, and when the page declares no doctype the text leaves open whether the particular case applies. Needs is empty: the elements, the doctype, styles and the accessibility tree are read on the page as loaded.
